retry: 3 at 5 s, then latch and annunciate

retry: 3 at 5 s, then latch and annunciate

retry: 3 at 5 s, then latch and annunciate

expression: A15 >= PARK, as TAIL_PARK (hold the previous state while PASS is active, and while A15 reads FAULT - D-410) - PWM at the dimmer's duty; never a door. O20 is the illumination bus only: the dash lamps, the head unit's illumination wire and the ICU's dimming reference (D-462). The dome lamp left the PMU for its factory circuit on the always-hot F12 and its own door switch, so its 1.5 s fade-in, 8 s fade-out and 10-minute cut (D-248) are dropped. Where the dimmer's duty comes from is the control panel's (D-409: a driver's control goes to the DCU panel)
retry: 3 at 5 s, then latch and annunciate

expression: popup_cycle OR window_req  (see the pop-up rule; window_req is any of the four window keys held in the DCU's 0x400 frame). A window_req is refused, not queued, while popup_cycle is true, and a pop-up command is refused while window_req is true or O1 reads above 20 A (rules motor-bus, R11)
retry: follows the consumer: during a pop-up cycle 1, then off and flag - a trip means an obstruction; during a window command only, 5 at 15 s, no latch - a window at its stop is a normal spike (D-357)

expression: A2 == LOW  \|\|  A2 == WASH  \|\|  (A2 == INT && int_timer)  \|\|  (wiper_latch && A3 not PARKED)  — braking ON
retry: 5 at 15 s, no latch - the stall timer governs

expression: A2 == HIGH
retry: 5 at 15 s, no latch - the stall timer governs

expression: A16 >= RUN — a steady feed; speed is set by the low-side final stage at L3-BLW on the DCU's own PWM output, ≥ 20 kHz (D-257 — the PMU's PWM tops out at 400 Hz); output DISABLED this build — no motor (K-023 · D-253)
retry: 5 at 15 s, no latch - the stall timer governs

expression: A16 >= ACC && panel_defog  - the panel key over CAN, with a HARD A16 floor read from the ladder and never from the bus, so a bag bumping the key with the car asleep cannot switch 11.5 A of grid (D-350). Live this build - the panel's defog key is this build's (D-374, D-442), the output moves at MG27; the grid's condition is CK21's (R10)
retry: 5 at 15 s, no latch - the stall timer governs

expression: A16 == START  \|\|  (ignition_on && prime_timer < 3 s, the timer starting when ignition_on rises)  \|\|  (ignition_on && oil_ok) — ignition_on is the IGNITION channel's own state, so the pump holds through a key-ladder fault exactly as ignition does and never outlives it (D-410). oil_ok means oil pressure above OIL_MIN. The sender is OPEN at 0 psi and its resistance falls as pressure rises (00-CAR SP-787) under the 100 Ω pull-up (D-260), so pressure above OIL_MIN is a raw A7 reading BELOW the OIL_MIN count: oil_ok latches when A7 < OIL_MIN and clears after 5 s of continuous A7 >= OIL_MIN, or when ignition_on goes false. An OPEN reading (A7 > 1000) is zero pressure, never a fault: oil_ok is false and the pump stops after the 3 s prime - a broken sender wire stops the engine and the cluster shows zero oil pressure (D-461, reversing D-249's fail-open for the open case). A short (A7 < 20) still counts as oil_ok as D-249 had it - not touched by D-461. OIL_MIN is read in the car at commissioning, never entered on the bench (D-249). No CAN term in this gate, ever (D-251). At the swap the comparison follows the sensor bought (engine HO04)
retry: 1 at 2 s, then off until the key leaves RUN

expression: On when A16 >= RUN. Off only after A16 has read a clean OFF or ACC for 200 ms. While A16 reads FAULT (open, short, or supply dead - rules ladder-decode) it holds its last state as long as oil_ok is true and drops when oil_ok clears; a FAULT never turns it on. Annunciate KEY FAULT while held - the key cannot stop the engine then, and the stop is the master disconnect (RC01) (D-410)
retry: 1 at 2 s, then off until the key leaves RUN

expression: A16 >= ACC || release_pulse || (ignition_on && oil_ok) - the last term keeps O10 on while the engine runs, whatever the key ladder or the low-voltage shed says, so the ICU on DP-ICU-A 1 stays up (D-463; rules voltage). release_pulse is short and self-clearing (hundreds of ms) and is raised only by the hatch or fuel-door release command, which the DCU refuses unless the car is stopped; the DCU drops its select after 1.5 s at most (D-465). The release relays K3 / K4 are fed through F33 (10 A) and are live whenever O10 is, so with the key on a select alone fires a solenoid - the protection is F33, the select pull-downs and that refusal, not the pulse (D-465 corrects D-370). It exists because both solenoids sit on O10 branches (D-180) and O10 was ACCESSORY: solving the panel's power did not solve the output (D-354). The other O10 consumers coming up for the length of the pulse is harmless
retry: 3 at 5 s, then latch and annunciate

expression: A8 == HORN  \|\|  A8 == HAZ+HORN
retry: 3 at 5 s, then latch and annunciate

expression: A16 >= RUN  (nothing connected this build)
retry: 3 at 5 s, then latch and annunciate

expression: A16 == START  &&  (A4 == CRANK_OK || A4 == TRANSIT+PN)
retry: 1 at 2 s, then off until the key leaves RUN

expression: self-hold: ON at any wake; OFF 30 s after the last input change with A16 == OFF, A6 == CLOSED and A8 == IDLE (hazards, horn or a wink hold it awake - rules flasher); forced OFF after 30 min with A16 == OFF whatever A6 reads (D-248) - EXCEPT while hazard is true: the hazard switch holds the car awake with no limit, past the 30-minute forced sleep, and the hazards flash until the pack's own protection cuts in (D-464). The forced-sleep timer restarts when the hazards go off
DISABLED. At the swap LS_FAN (O14) switches the radiator fan relay's coil, never the fan current - the fan has its own relay and fuse off the battery side (D-468)
